type: Original podcast concept and visual identity
headline: Real talk. Real laughs. Real perspectives.
narrative: Chit-Chat began as an idea of my own. I envisioned a podcast where everyday conversations could be honest, hilarious, thought-provoking, and occasionally serious, without the weight of political debate. I wanted to create a space where different opinions could be expressed openly, facts could be acknowledged, and humor could always find its way into the conversation. That personality became the inspiration behind the visual identity. I designed the logo around a speech bubble, giving conversation a recognizable visual home. Looking closely at the C reveals a playful detail inspired by the familiar “clock it” finger gesture—a subtle nod to recognizing what's being said and calling attention to the moment. With bold yellow, black, and white, I created an identity that feels expressive, confident, and unapologetically conversational. Because sometimes the best conversations are the ones where everyone gets to speak, laugh, and be heard.
